Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can keep momentum: 

Recap of discovery:
- Primary use case: generate executive summaries and action items from multi-hour customer call transcripts (~100k tokens).
- Key constraints: preserve verbatim quoting for compliance, minimize truncation losses, and keep latency for summaries under 3s for 4k-window live use (batch jobs reasonable at higher latency).
- Evaluation priorities: summarization fidelity, entity preservation, truncation behavior for very long histories, and hallucination/regression detection.

Redwood recommendations (high level):
1) Models: redwood-llama-70b-8k as the baseline for long-context fidelity; consider redwood-llama-70b-32k or our long-context variant (rc-70b-32k) for the ~100k token offline jobs (we recommend segmentation + overlap for >32k). For lower cost, try rc-13b-32k quantized.
2) Approach: hybrid pipeline — use chunked encoding with an overlap window + KV cache for live streams, and a denser offline pass (32k/64k chunks) for final summaries.
3) Prompts & evals: we ran an initial eval on your sample transcript. I’ve attached the prompt set (prompt-set-v1.jsonl) and the CSV of results (acme-long-context-eval-results.csv). Key finding: models truncate differently when system messages are long; we saw entity omission around chunk boundaries in 12% of samples for the 8k model.

Next steps we propose:
- Share the full prompt set + eval CSV (attached) — you can run these locally or we can run another pass.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi (infrastructure) to review integration, KV cache behavior, and latency SLOs. 
- If you want, we can produce a short POC (1–2 transcripts) using rc-70b-32k segmented pipeline to show summarization fidelity and truncation behavior.

Would you be available for a 45-min technical deep-dive next week? Thursday or Friday afternoon (PDT) works for our engineering team.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Hi Alex — answers inline + attachments called out:

1) Strategy: our recommended default is a two-pass approach for >32k transcripts:
   - Pass 1 (chunked, overlap 10–20%): extract per-chunk highlights and canonical entities.
   - Pass 2 (consolidation): synthesize a coherent executive summary from the per-chunk outputs, preserving entity links and timestamps.
   This reduces boundary hallucinations and preserves decision/action items more reliably than a single-pass chunk->summarize without consolidation. In our evals, consolidation reduced entity-drop by ~60% vs naive chunk summarization (see attached CSV).

2) Metric: for CEO-level fidelity we recommend a composite of ROUGE-L + an entity-preservation score (we computed exact-match for named entities and a custom action-item precision). The CSV includes these columns — the action-item precision aligned best with manual QA for your samples.

3) Cost: rough ballpark (processing + inference): rc-70b-32k POC workload ~ $8k–$12k/mo for 200 completions/day at your average output size (assuming batching and our caching defaults). rc-13b-32k quantized ~ $2k–$3k/mo. We’ll refine with exact token counts in the deep-dive.

Attaching: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (examples for chunk & consolidation prompts), acme-long-context-eval-results.csv (metrics), redwood-model-recommendation.pdf (deltas & quantization tradeoffs).

We can do Friday 2026-07-01 1:00–1:45 PM PDT. Rishi and Dev are available and I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm.

Best,
—Marissa
